newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah to resume Katyusha attacks on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah to resume Katyusha attacks on Israel.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah said on Friday it would resume Katyusha rocket attacks on northern Israel because a 1996 ceasefire understanding had failed to protect Lebanese civilians.

"We say the understanding has ceased to protect civilians. We say the resumption of using other means to protect civilians has become necessary," Hizbollah secretary-general Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah told a news conference.
"But the timing of using Katyushas to protect civilians has to do with the situation on the ground...and a number of other similar considerations," he said.
Katyusha rockets fired by guerrillas in Lebanon slammed into a northern Israeli town early on Friday, slightly injuring a woman and damaging a synagogue, the Israeli military said.
Nasrallah said Hizbollah was not responsible for the attack.
"When we fire Katyushas towards northern Palestine, we claim responsibility. We have a history that testifies to that. We don't fire at night and hide in the morning," he said.
A 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people -- mainly Lebanese civilians -- were killed, barred Hizbollah guerrillas and Israeli troops from targeting civilians.
Israel launched the offensive to stop Hizbollah guerrillas from firing rockets into its northern areas.
Nasrallah's comments came during the bloodiest week in south Lebanon since the Israeli onslaught.
Since Monday, 13 people have died in cross-border violence, including seven civilans, starting with an Israeli commando raid in which five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed with a roadside bomb.
Hizbollah threatened to carry out suicide bombings inside Israel and Arab land occupied by the Jewish state during a funeral procession for the five guerrillas.
Nasrallah said any future Israeli offensives would target Syria, which has some 35,000 troops stationed in Lebanon.
"If the Israelis are preparing for war, any new war will not target Hizbollah and the resistance. Its target will be Syria in specific," Nasrallah said.
"It will aim at creating new conditions in favour of a (peace) settlement and to impose Israel's and America's terms in the region," he added.
Syria, the main power broker in Lebanon, and the Beirut government closely coordinate peace moves.
Peace talks have been stalled over an Israeli refusal to withdraw from the Syrian Golan Heights captured in 1967 and a south Lebanon area occupied since 1978.
Nasrallah said Israel's latest attacks against civilians in Lebanon aimed at wrecking the April 1996 U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
"The developments in the south aim at abolishing the April understanding through continuous Israeli violations," he said.

Nasrallah criticised a five-nation monitoring committee comprising the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel, saying "it has become a committee of statistics for the number of the dead and wounded".
